story.title: French Navy Intercepts Tanker Linked to Russia's Shadow Fleet
story.summary: The French Navy has seized an oil tanker in the Indian Ocean, suspected of being part of Russia's shadow fleet. Footage shows the Navy boarding and escorting the vessel as part of ongoing efforts to enforce sanctions against Russia.

event_overview.title: About Russia Sanctions
event_overview.subject: Russia Sanctions
event_overview.summary: The relevant legislative event is the Countering America’s Adversaries Through Sanctions Act (CAATSA), a U.S. law that created and expanded sanctions authorities concerning Iran, Russia, and North Korea. Its Russia provisions form one component of the broader U.S. Russia-sanctions framework, alongside authorities created by executive orders and other statutes.

facts.label: Legislative dates
facts.value: H.R. 3364 passed the House on July 25, 2017, passed the Senate on July 27, 2017, and became Public Law 115-44 on August 2, 2017.

facts.label: Legal scope
facts.value: CAATSA is organized into separate titles addressing Iran, the Russian Federation, and North Korea; Title II addresses Russia-related sanctions and measures concerning terrorism and illicit financing.

facts.label: Stated purpose
facts.value: The enacted law states that it provides for congressional review and counters aggression by the governments of Iran, the Russian Federation, and North Korea.

facts.label: Administration
facts.value: The Treasury Department’s Office of Foreign Assets Control administers CAATSA-related sanctions; OFAC identifies CAATSA as implemented through Public Law 115-44 and Executive Order 13849.

facts.label: Relation to wider Russia sanctions
facts.value: CAATSA is not the only U.S. Russia-sanctions authority: OFAC separately lists Russian Harmful Foreign Activities and Ukraine-/Russia-related sanctions programs, among others.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline highlights particular sanctions and maritime-enforcement developments, but does not provide a complete history of U.S. Russia sanctions; its September 2026 House-passage title should not be read as the date of CAATSA’s actual 2017 congressional passage.

related_stories.title: Saudi Arabia Faces Houthi Attacks on Energy Facilities
related_stories.summary: Saudi Arabia is experiencing increased pressure from Houthi attacks targeting airports and energy facilities. The Iran-aligned Houthi militia has threatened to strike the Saudi energy giant Aramco following an evacuation notice issued by Saudi authorities for an oil facility in Yemen's capital. This situation raises questions about the potential success of a Saudi-led international military offensive against the Houthis.

related_stories.title: Saudi Arabia Suspends Flights Following Houthi Missile Attacks on Riyadh Airport
related_stories.summary: Saudi Arabia has suspended all flights to and from King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh until next Saturday due to a series of Houthi missile attacks. The latest attack resulted in at least 13 fatalities and numerous injuries, prompting heightened security concerns. CCTV footage captured the moment of the missile strike, which has raised questions about the effectiveness of the country's defenses against such threats.

related_stories.title: Zelenskyy Claims No Warning from Allies Before Russian Missile Strikes on Kyiv
related_stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that Kyiv did not receive any early warning from its allies regarding a Russian ballistic missile strike that hit civilian infrastructure. He described the attack as 'particularly vile' and emphasized the importance of intelligence sharing for saving lives. Despite concerns about potential halts in intelligence sharing, officials indicated that the U.S. continues to provide support.
